newsitem.title: CHINA: Killer typhoon Winnie hits China.
newsitem.headline: Killer typhoon Winnie hits China.

text.p: Strong winds and high water killed several people, toppled houses and flooded towns as Typhoon Winnie slammed into eastern China, local officials said on Tuesday.
The typhoon hit the eastern province of Zhejiang at 9.30 p.m. (1330 GMT) on Monday, the Xinhua news agency said.
Detailed damage reports were not immediately available but local officials said several people were killed and many more injured as the typhoon battered Zhejiang's cities and towns.

Powerful waves battered down a sea wall and capsized boats in Wenling city, where the typhoon made landfall, and floods washed through the city, damaging about 1,000 houses, said an official of the municipal flood control headquarters.
At least one person in the city was killed, the official said, but gave no details.
In Jinhua city, about 200 km (120 miles) inland, floods ravaged a municipal county. At least one person was killed and the typhoon continued to rage on Tuesday morning, officials said.
Officials also reported deaths in the provincial capital of Hangzhou, but they declined to give details.
Shortly after the typhoon arrived, Chinese President Jiang Zemin had ordered officials to fight the typhoon and to take part in relief work to minimise losses, Xinhua said.
"Jiang Zemin... and Chinese Premier Li Peng extended their cordial regards to locals right after the landing," the official agency said.
Typhoon Winnie on Monday and Tuesday killed 25 people in Taiwan, where landslides brought down buildings and floodwaters turned streets into rivers, Taiwan officials said.
The Taiwan government's anti-typhoon centre said one person was missing, 16 seriously injured and 62 slightly hurt.
